title: Palo Alto Networks Certified Network Security Associate (PCNSA)

nodes.title: Security Profiles: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Security Profiles. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A security policy rule allows web-browsing traffic. The admin also attaches an Antivirus profile and a Vulnerability Protection profile to the same rule. Which statement best describes this configuration?
flashcards.back: Security policy rules determine allow or deny. Security profiles (AV, Anti-Spyware, Vulnerability Protection, etc.) define what happens to traffic that the policy permits — they inspect it for threats and can reset, drop, or alert on individual threat events without necessarily blocking the entire session. The two constructs are complementary, not redundant. the attached profiles inspect the permitted traffic for threats without affecting the allow decision

flashcards.front: Which security profile is specifically designed to detect traffic from an already-infected internal host attempting to reach a command-and-control server on the internet?
flashcards.back: Anti-Spyware profiles target the outbound C2 communication stage of an attack — when an already-infected host attempts to beacon or receive commands from an external controller. Vulnerability Protection protects against inbound exploits. Antivirus scans file content. WildFire analyzes unknown files, not established C2 traffic patterns.

flashcards.front: A security admin creates multiple security rules that each require the same six security profiles (AV, Anti-Spyware, Vulnerability Protection, URL Filtering, File Blocking, WildFire). What Palo Alto construct reduces management overhead and ensures consistency?
flashcards.back: A Security Profile Group bundles multiple individual profiles (AV, Anti-Spyware, Vulnerability Protection, URL Filtering, File Blocking, WildFire) into a named group. Applying the group to a rule is a single selection, and updating the group propagates changes to all rules using it — greatly reducing effort compared to updating six individual profiles per rule.

flashcards.front: A network admin configures a Vulnerability Protection profile with action 'block-ip' for high-severity signatures. What does 'block-ip' do differently from 'drop'?
flashcards.back: The 'block-ip' action in threat profiles dynamically adds the offending source IP to a block list for a configurable period (e.g., 300 seconds), preventing all subsequent connections from that IP during the block window. 'Drop' silently discards the offending packet/session. 'Reset-client' or 'reset-server' sends TCP RST. 'block-ip' is more aggressive, effectively quarantining the attacker. preventing all future traffic from that IP for a configured duration

nodes.title: VPN and secure connectivity: Key Ideas
nodes.content: A VPN tunnels private traffic over the public internet, encrypting it end-to-end. Site-to-site VPNs connect networks (e.g., on-prem to cloud); client VPNs connect individual devices to a private network. Both rely on IPsec or SSL/TLS.

flashcards.front: Site-to-site VPN vs client VPN — what's the difference?
flashcards.back: Site-to-site VPN connects two networks (typical: on-prem data center ↔ cloud VPC) using gateway devices on each side. Client VPN connects an individual user's laptop to a private network for remote access. Site-to-site uses IPsec, client VPN often uses SSL or WireGuard.

Phase 1 (IKE) authenticates the two peers (pre-shared key or certificate) and builds a secure management channel. Phase 2 negotiates the actual data tunnel (encryption algorithm, key lifetime). Most exam questions test that phase 1 must succeed before phase 2.

flashcards.front: When do you pick a dedicated link over a VPN?
flashcards.back: VPN over the public internet is cheap but variable — bandwidth and latency depend on internet weather. Dedicated links (Direct Connect, ExpressRoute, Cloud Interconnect) are private fiber with consistent latency and bandwidth — pick them for production traffic that must be predictable, or compliance scenarios that forbid the public internet.

flashcards.front: What's the BGP tunnel option for?
flashcards.back: VPNs can use static routes or BGP. BGP-based VPNs auto-propagate route changes between sides (add a new subnet on-prem → cloud learns it within seconds). Static VPN requires manual route updates every time the topology changes. Always pick BGP for production.

pairs.prompt: Dynamic IP and Port (DIPP/PAT), where many internal hosts share one public IP distinguished by source port configure to allow hundreds of internal hosts (10.0.0.0/8) to share a single public IP address for internet access.

Active/Active HA, where both firewalls forward traffic simultaneously and share the session table state provides automatic failover to a standby unit while only one firewall actively processes traffic at a time.

The purpose of a Palo Alto service object set to 'application-default' versus 'any' in a security policy rule is 'Application-default' restricts the rule to the ports PAN-OS expects for the specified application id.

Layer 2 mode, where the firewall acts as a transparent bridge between VLANs and enforces policy on the bridge allows the firewall to inspect traffic at Layer 2 by bridging VLANs while also performing security policy enforcement.
